conservation_status.value: critically low, about 250 birds in conservancy as of 2021; listed by the FAO

origin_year_or_period.value: estimated to have arisen in the mid-third century

value: males can grow tails up to 1.5 meters (4.9 ft) long
tail feathers molt annually after the rainy season, unlike Japan's Onagadori

history_summary.value: An ancient Korean heritage breed famous for its extremely long tail feathers, nearly wiped out in the early 1900s by the rise of commercial non-native chicken farming. It survived thanks to one dedicated farmer, and as of 2021 only about 250 birds remained in conservation.
